sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Osmunda japonica is an East Asian fern with bipinnate fronds reaching about 150 × 50 cm. It grows in moist woodland habitats.

sections.title: Fronds and spores
sections.text: The fertile fronds differ from sterile fronds in having narrow pinnae covered in sporangia. Young fronds are coiled before they unfurl.

sections.title: Food use
sections.text: In Japan, young shoots known as zenmai are eaten after cooking. This does not document raw consumption.
